description: We are Code Reaper, participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We are developing ASTROCARE, an AI-powered health monitoring and rehabilitation platform for astronauts on long-duration space missions. Our solution helps astronauts track vital signs, monitor physical and mental well-being, identify potential health risks, and receive safe, personalized guidance. Our mission is to use AI and technology to support astronaut health and make future space exploration safer.
summary:
CODE REAPER is a predictive, AI-driven health intelligence and rehabilitation platform designed for deep-space astronauts. Addressing the challenge of human health in long-duration missions, it goes beyond reactive monitoring by creating a "Digital Twin" of the astronaut. 

Our solution integrates three core innovations: First, a 3D Digital Twin Simulator that calculates biomechanical loads and predicts injury risks (e.g., spinal compression) before exercises are executed, enforcing deterministic medical safety protocols. Second, a Gemini-powered AI Mental Wellness companion that provides empathetic, voice-enabled psychological support to combat isolation. Third, an interactive 3D symptom mapping and unified telemetry dashboard linked directly to a Flight Surgeon Command Center. 

Grounded in official NASA HRP and CSA data (including live NASA DONKI space weather telemetry), CODE REAPER ensures that astronauts are not just monitored, but actively protected and rehabilitated. It bridges the gap between Earth-based medicine and the extreme environment of the cosmos, ensuring crew safety for Artemis and future Mars missions.
details:
CODE REAPER is a predictive, full-stack health intelligence and rehabilitation platform designed for deep-space astronauts (Artemis missions). The project addresses the critical need for autonomous medical support during long-duration spaceflight, where real-time communication with Earth is delayed.

How it works: The platform features a React/Node.js frontend and backend, utilizing a 3D Interactive Anatomical Body for symptom mapping, a "Digital Twin Simulator" that calculates biomechanical loads (e.g., spinal compression) to predict injury risks before exercises, and an AI-powered Mental Wellness Companion (using Groq/OpenRouter APIs) for psychological support. It also includes a unified Medical Timeline and a Flight Surgeon Dashboard for role-based monitoring and approval workflows.

Benefits & Impact: It shifts astronaut healthcare from reactive to predictive. By simulating the physical consequences of actions (like lifting heavy loads in microgravity), it prevents injuries (e.g., disc herniation) before they happen. The mental wellness component combats isolation, and the dual-dashboard system ensures seamless coordination between the astronaut in orbit and the flight surgeon on the ground.

Tools & Technologies: React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Node.js (Express), Firebase (Authentication & Firestore for role-based access), Three.js/React Three Fiber (for 3D rendering), Recharts (for telemetry visualization), and Gemini/Groq LLMs for AI reasoning.
